hints: Focus on what a catalytic converter is for, turning two harmful exhaust gases into harmless gases you already find in clean air.
Notice that $\text{NO}$ must be reduced, so nitrogen should end up as harmless $\text{N}_2$, not as $\text{NO}_2$ which is still a pollutant.
Pair that with oxidation of toxic $\text{CO}$ to $\text{CO}_2$, then pick the equation where both pollutants disappear together.
walkthrough:
**Recall the job of the catalytic converter**

Think of it as a clean up unit. It must remove both carbon monoxide, $\text{CO}$, and nitrogen monoxide, $\text{NO}$, at the same time.

It does this by a redox reaction: $\text{CO}$ is oxidised and $\text{NO}$ is reduced.

**Decide the harmless products**

Reduction of $\text{NO}$ means removing oxygen from nitrogen. The safe product is nitrogen gas, $\text{N}_2$, which makes up most of clean air.

Any equation that still makes $\text{NO}_2$ is not helpful, because $\text{NO}_2$ is also a toxic pollutant.

**Decide what happens to carbon monoxide**

Oxidation of $\text{CO}$ means adding oxygen. The product is carbon dioxide, $\text{CO}_2$, which is far less toxic than $\text{CO}$.

It should not make solid carbon, $\text{C(s)}$, which would block the converter.

Correct overall change:
$$2\text{NO(g)} + 2\text{CO(g)} \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$

**Match to the options**

Only one equation converts both $\text{NO}$ to $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{CO}$ to $\text{CO}_2$ with all atoms balanced. That is the reaction that decreases $\text{NO}$ emission.

options.A: Incorrect. This makes $\text{NO}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{C(s)}$. $\text{NO}_2$ is still a harmful nitrogen oxide pollutant, so $\text{NO}$ emission is not solved, and solid carbon would deposit on the catalyst.
options.B: Incorrect. This consumes $\text{CO}_2$ to make $\text{CO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$. That is backwards, it creates toxic $\text{CO}$ and keeps nitrogen as a pollutant $\text{NO}_2$ instead of harmless $\text{N}_2$.
options.C: Correct. $\text{NO}$ is reduced to harmless $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{CO}$ is oxidised to $\text{CO}_2$. Both pollutants are removed together in one balanced redox reaction, which is exactly what the rhodium catalyst does.
options.D: Incorrect. This makes $2\text{NO}_2$ from $2\text{NO}$, so nitrogen stays as a pollutant oxide, and it also makes $\text{C(s)}$. It does not produce harmless $\text{N}_2$ and does not remove $\text{CO}$.
